title: Microsoft Purview: adaptive scope lifecycle status controls for recipients and site owners (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned government-cloud control and distinguishes it from existing adaptive-scope tools. The documented paths, commands and retention-policy licensing are supported; the new control's default and configuration remain unpublished. One checklist step asks readers to review role assignments without a corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: An adaptive scope uses a query to define dynamic membership of users, Microsoft 365 groups or sites.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so you can define the membership of users or groups included in that query. ... There are three different types of adaptive scopes

claims.claim: Communication compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies can use adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy.

claims.claim: Communication compliance policies do not support SharePoint sites or OneDrive accounts in adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: For communication compliance policies: SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts aren't supported.

claims.claim: IsInactiveMailbox is the documented OPATH property for excluding or targeting inactive mailboxes, not a documented site-owner lifecycle filter.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes. For this configuration, use the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox

claims.claim: Excluding or targeting inactive mailboxes requires the advanced query builder.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes.

claims.claim: Users without a valid licence for adaptive scopes do not have the policy settings applied to them.

claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.claim: Existing adaptive-scope queries and query changes can take up to five days to fully populate or become effective.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.claim: The member details list can take up to five days to reflect added or removed members.

claims.claim: The Purview portal route Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder reaches scope-query configuration.

claims.quote: Use the New-AdaptiveScope cmdlet to create adaptive scopes ... -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> ... Valid values are: User ... The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode.

claims.claim: An administrator not restricting the adaptive scope by administrative unit should keep Full directory.
claims.quote: If you don't want to restrict the adaptive scope by using administrative units, or your organization hasn't configured administrative units, keep the default of Full directory.
